name: Haiku macro/sector rotation
strategy: Rotate from defensive to conviction macro: deploy cash into energy (42% YTD), financials (rate beneficiaries), healthcare (earnings turnaround), and crypto recovery, while eliminating utilities which are uncompetitive vs rising Treasury yields.
reassessment_note: Week delivered three key shifts: (1) Geopolitical shock (Iran/Strait) resolved into mid-week rally, proving market resilience; (2) Fed messaging now 57% priced for September hike, making utilities (2.6% yield vs 4.8% Treasuries) untenable and financials compelling; (3) Sector rotation broadened beyond tech into energy (+42% YTD at 13x P/E cheapest), healthcare (+24% 1yr momentum), small caps, and value. Current 62.79% cash is opportunity cost; deployed selectively into proven winners (BTC +27% week, XLV +5.48% leg) and macro tailwinds. Utilities eliminated entirely. Dry powder reduced from 62.79% to 10% for post-earnings optionality.

positions.thesis: Crypto recovery cycle intact; +27% this week on Fed pause signals and $3.33B spot ETF monthly inflows. Funding rate only 10% on longs now sustainable. Bitcoin near $81k represents break above key resistance; Sept 15-18 window (Clarity Act vote, Fed decision) should determine next leg. Allocation captures momentum while sizing for volatility.

Healthcare is the strongest sector pivot: +24% 1-year return, +14% 3-month momentum, strong earnings revisions. XLV leg up +5.48% this week. Sector mean-reverting after 2023-2024 weakness; provides diversification from tech and earnings growth visibility. 3x position size increase from 6.71% justified by turnaround thesis.

Small cap broadening rotation confirmed this week: market leadership extending from mega-cap tech into IWM, signaling health of rally. IWM +1.65% leg, benefiting from industrials and financials strength. Russell 2000 participation in leadership change is macro-positive. Position increased 36% from 10.98%.

Energy sector is 2026's macro leader: +42% YTD vs SPY +22%, cheapest valuation at 13x P/E with 2.4% dividend yield. Geopolitical tensions (Strait of Hormuz) support supply premium; AI infrastructure demand for power structural. Sept 1 shock resolved positively, confirming supply is resilient. First new position; 10% allocation is entry-sized.

Financials positioned perfectly for 2026 macro: steeper yield curve (2yr-10yr 40bps, 10yr at 4.8%), rising long-term rates expand net interest margins. September 25bp hike now priced 57%, extending tightening cycle extends this benefit. Capital markets activity improving. Upward earnings revisions across sector. 9% allocation captures rate duration play.

Maintains core AI/semis exposure; QQQ +4.50% leg and +22.3% Q3 earnings growth expected for Nasdaq 100. Position reduced from 7.32% (small trim) as rotation favors value, but tech earnings remain robust. AI infrastructure theme still intact. Lower weighting reflects macro rotation rather than conviction loss.

Gold +9.48% leg; inflation hedge still relevant despite rising real yields. Trimmed from 6.1% to 3% as portfolio now has better inflation optionality (energy, financials benefit from higher nominal growth). Maintains diversification at reduced opportunity cost.
